PLAN "Postpartum Return — 12 Week Progressive Reconditioning"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Rebuild foundational strength and mobility postpartum"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (Postpartum weeks 4–7)" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 30m "Gentle return walk + mobility":
        warmup:
          walking 10m
        main straight_sets:
          marching 3x30 seconds rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          pelvic_tilt 3x10 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          bird_dog 3x6..8 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 5m
      DAY Wednesday training 30m "Low-impact conditioning + posterior activation":
        warmup:

        main straight_sets:

NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Aim for an additional ~450 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy needs to support breastfeeding, adjusted to appetite and weight change."
    - "Prioritise protein ~1.1–1.3 g/kg bodyweight per day through meals and snacks."
    - "Include a variety of nutrient-dense foods: whole grains, lean protein, dairy or calcium-rich alternatives, legumes, fruits, vegetables, nuts, and seeds."
    - "Hydrate regularly: aim for fluid when feeding and throughout the day; include water with each meal and snack."
    - "Ensure iron-rich foods and vitamin C to aid absorption; consider continued prenatal/postnatal multivitamin as advised by her provider."
    - "Distribute calories across 3 meals + 2–3 snacks to support energy for breastfeeding and training."
    - "Avoid aggressive calorie restriction while breastfeeding; steady gradual weight change only if desired and approved by her clinician."
    - "Monitor infant weight gain and maternal energy — adjust intake if milk supply or maternal fatigue changes."
    - "On HIIT and heavy training days, ensure adequate calories and fluids; consider timing sessions when baby is settled and plan feeds to reduce engorgement discomfort."
    - "Stop or regress training and seek clinician/physio review if increased pelvic pressure, abdominal doming/bulging, wound tenderness, unusual bleeding, dizziness, or drop in milk supply occur."
    - "If she has dietary restrictions or concerns, refer to a registered dietitian specialising in postpartum/breastfeeding."
